ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Context-ablation likelihood shifts as utilization signals for RAG hallucination detection
PROPOSAL: Define external utilization E as the drop in the response's mean token log-likelihood when the retrieved passages are removed from the prompt, and internal utilization I as the log-likelihood the same model gives the response under a closed-book prompt. Generate responses with Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct and Mistral-7B-Instruct on RAGTruth (question answering, summarization, data-to-text), obtain both signals from 2 forward passes per response, and train a logistic regression on E, I and their difference using the response-level labels. Score with a model that differs from the generator and report AUROC and F1 on held-out splits per task type.
CONTROLS: Compare against mean token entropy, perplexity of the response given the context, a ReDeEP reproduction with its published head and layer choices, and a judge-prompt baseline. Drop E, drop I, and drop the difference in turn; use 10 seeds for the regression splits.
COST: 60
PREDICTION: The combined signal should lead either alone by 3 to 6 AUROC points; it could fail on data-to-text, where closed-book likelihood barely moves with the table content.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Two-pass logit contrast between context-conditioned and closed-book decoding for RAG hallucination scoring
PROPOSAL: For each response token, take the log-probability gap between a context-conditioned prompt and a closed-book prompt, and summarize it as E (probability mass moved toward context-supported tokens) and I (mass kept on tokens the closed-book pass already prefers). Run Llama-3.3-70B-Instruct as generator and scorer on the RAGTruth question-answering subset only, over 5 context variants (full passages, top-1 passage, shuffled passages, sentence-dropped passages, truncated passages) per example, and fit a gradient-boosted classifier on the aggregated signals with 10 fits from different seeds. Report AUROC and F1 on the held-out split.
CONTROLS: Compare against mean token entropy, perplexity of the response given the context, a ReDeEP reproduction with its published head and layer choices, and a judge-prompt baseline. Drop E, drop I, and compare the 5 context variants with the single full-context contrast.
COST: 60
PREDICTION: The contrast should reach an AUROC of 0.80 or higher on question answering; it could fail if the 70B model's closed-book pass is so confident that I saturates over responses.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Proxy-model scoring of context and parametric reliance across generators
PROPOSAL: Compute E as the average gain in response log-likelihood from adding the retrieved passages to a bare query, and I as the average log-likelihood of the response with no passages, using a single proxy scorer, Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct, on responses written by 6 generators in RAGTruth. Fit a small logistic regression on responses from 3 generators and test on the 3 unseen ones, holding out 20 percent of items, then repeat with the proxy replaced by the generator's own weights where those are public. Report AUROC and F1 per generator and the gap between proxy scoring and self scoring.
CONTROLS: Compare against perplexity under the proxy, token entropy of the proxy, a response-only classifier trained on the same split, and a ReDeEP reproduction run on the open generators. Drop E and drop I in turn; use 3 seeds for the split of generators.
COST: 150
PREDICTION: Proxy scoring should lose under 4 AUROC points relative to self scoring; it could fail for closed generators whose style differs sharply from the proxy's own.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Utilization scores from a 32B scorer over retrieval datasets
PROPOSAL: Compute E as the average gain in response log-likelihood from adding the retrieved passages to a bare query, and I as the average log-likelihood of the response with no passages, using Qwen2.5-32B-Instruct as scorer on responses from an 8B generator in RAGTruth, HaluEval question answering and a news summarization set with sentence-level labels. Fit a logistic regression on each dataset separately, then test transfer by training on one dataset and testing on the others. Report AUROC and F1 for the train-test pairs, averaged over 5 resplits.
CONTROLS: Compare against perplexity under the scorer, token entropy of the scorer, a response-only classifier trained on the same split, and a ReDeEP reproduction on the 8B generator. Drop E and drop I in turn; compare the 32B scorer with the generator's own weights on RAGTruth, using 3 seeds.
COST: 150
PREDICTION: Transfer should lose under 5 AUROC points relative to in-dataset training; it could fail on the summarization set, where the labels mark finer spans than the other 2 sets.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Replacing attention-head selection with a single layer-free attribution signal
PROPOSAL: Measure E as the share of the response's attribution mass, from integrated gradients on the input embeddings, that falls on retrieved passage tokens, and I as the attribution mass on the query tokens and the generated prefix. Run on 400 responses from Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct in the RAGTruth question-answering subset, with 50 interpolation steps, and compare the share ratio between labeled hallucinated and supported responses. Report AUROC of the ratio, plus its rank correlation with the response-level label, on a held-out split of 100 responses. Repeat the whole pipeline for Mistral-7B-Instruct to check that no model-specific choice was needed.
CONTROLS: Compare against mean token entropy, response perplexity given the context, and the attention-mass share on passage tokens averaged over all heads. Score a shuffled-passage version of 100 responses to check that E falls when the context is unrelated; use 3 seeds for the held-out draw.
COST: 36
PREDICTION: The ratio should reach an AUROC near 0.70; it could fail because gradient attributions are noisy for short responses with fewer than 20 tokens.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Occlusion-window sensitivity of response likelihood to passage and query spans
PROPOSAL: Measure E as the drop in the response's log-likelihood when windows of passage tokens are masked out, and I as the drop when query tokens are masked instead, using Llama-3.1-70B-Instruct on 400 responses from the RAGTruth question-answering subset. Slide windows of 4 to 64 tokens with stride 2 and compare the ratio of E to I between labeled hallucinated and supported responses at the best window length. Report AUROC of the ratio and its rank correlation with the label on a held-out split of 100 responses, then repeat the sliding procedure with a second scorer to see whether window choices carry over.
CONTROLS: Compare against mean token entropy, response perplexity given the context, and the attention-mass share on passage tokens averaged over all heads. Score a shuffled-passage version of 100 responses to check that E falls when the context is unrelated; use 3 seeds for the held-out draw.
COST: 36
PREDICTION: The ratio should reach an AUROC near 0.70; it could fail when passages are long and short windows leave answers unchanged.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Counterfactual conflict sets that test whether E and I track context use and parametric use
PROPOSAL: Build a conflict set from Natural Questions by replacing the gold entity in the retrieved passage with a plausible wrong entity (2000 items), generate answers with Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct, Mistral-7B-Instruct and Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct, and label each answer as following the passage, following the model's memory, or neither. Compute E from log-likelihood gain when the passage is supplied and I from the closed-book log-likelihood. Check that E is higher for passage-following answers than for memory-following ones and that I shows the reverse, then train a logistic detector on the swapped set and apply it unchanged to RAGTruth. Report AUROC, F1 and effect sizes per model.
CONTROLS: Compare against attention-mass and entropy-based indicators, a ReDeEP reproduction with published head and layer choices, and a judge-prompt baseline. Run a null where the swapped entity is irrelevant to the question, with 5 seeds for the detector fit.
COST: 300
PREDICTION: E and I should separate the 3 answer types with effect sizes above 0.5; it could fail for Qwen if its memory of the swapped entities is weak, leaving few memory-following answers.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Utilization signals from a conflict set built for a single dataset with a 70B generator
PROPOSAL: Build a conflict set from Natural Questions by replacing the gold entity in the retrieved passage with a plausible wrong entity (4000 items), generate answers with Llama-3.1-70B-Instruct (greedy decoding, 1 sample per item), and label each answer as following the passage, following the model's memory, or neither. Compute E from log-likelihood gain when the passage is supplied and I from the closed-book log-likelihood. Repeat the whole pipeline for 10 entity-swap draws with different random seeds, check that E is higher for passage-following answers than for memory-following ones and that I shows the reverse, and fit a logistic detector on each draw. Report AUROC, F1 and effect sizes averaged over the draws.
CONTROLS: Compare against attention-mass and entropy-based indicators, a ReDeEP reproduction with published head and layer choices, and a judge-prompt baseline. Run a null where the swapped entity is irrelevant to the question; keep the detector fit and held-out split fixed.
COST: 300
PREDICTION: E and I should separate the 3 answer types with effect sizes above 0.5; it could fail if the 70B model follows the passage so often that few memory-following answers remain.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Quantile pooling of token-level E and I trajectories for summarization hallucination detection
PROPOSAL: Compute token-level E as the log-likelihood gain from the retrieved document and token-level I as the closed-book log-likelihood, then summarize each response with the lower quartile, median and upper quartile instead of a mean, plus the longest run of tokens where I exceeds E. Use Llama-3.1-8B summaries of news articles from the RAGTruth summarization split and the CNN/DailyMail test set with 300 sampled articles, and fit a logistic regression on the pooled features. Report AUROC and F1 with the response-level labels, and check how the detector's score changes when summaries are cut to the first 3 sentences.
CONTROLS: Compare against mean pooling of the same signals, mean token entropy, response perplexity given the document, and a ReDeEP reproduction with its published head and layer choices. Run 5 seeds for the split and drop the run-length feature in turn.
COST: 90
PREDICTION: Quantile features should gain about 2 AUROC points over mean pooling; it could fail because long summaries dilute the few tokens that carry the unsupported claim.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Pooling functions for token-level E and I tracked over scorer models
PROPOSAL: Compute token-level E as the log-likelihood gain from the retrieved document and token-level I as the closed-book log-likelihood, then summarize each response with 12 pooling functions (mean, median, minimum, maximum, lower and upper quartiles, variance, and run-length statistics). Use summaries from the RAGTruth summarization split scored by open models from 7B to 32B parameters, and fit a logistic regression on the pooled features for each scorer separately. Report AUROC and F1 against the response-level labels, and rank the 12 functions by their stability across scorers.
CONTROLS: Compare against mean token entropy, response perplexity given the document, and a ReDeEP reproduction with its published head and layer choices. Run 3 seeds for the split and compare the best pooling function with the mean of the same signals.
COST: 90
PREDICTION: The best function should gain about 2 AUROC points over the mean; it could fail because the ranking of functions may change from one scorer to the next.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Detection under insufficient retrieval: dropping the key sentence from the passages
PROPOSAL: Take 500 question-answering items from RAGTruth where the passages support the answer, and make an insufficient variant by deleting the single sentence that contains the answer span. Let Llama-3.1-8B answer both versions, compute E from the log-likelihood gain of the passages and I from the closed-book log-likelihood, and train a logistic detector on the sufficient versions only. Apply it to the insufficient versions and report AUROC, F1 and the shift of E and I between versions. Break results down by whether the closed-book answer was already correct, to see when I drives the score.
CONTROLS: Compare against mean token entropy, response perplexity given the passages, and a ReDeEP reproduction with its published head and layer choices. Use 10 seeds for the detector fit and score a variant where a random sentence is removed instead of the key one.
COST: 48
PREDICTION: E should drop and I should rise on the insufficient versions, with detection AUROC staying above 0.70; it could fail when the model's memory happens to be right and its answers are labeled supported.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Insufficient-retrieval stress test on 70B with repeated key-sentence deletions
PROPOSAL: Take 500 question-answering items from RAGTruth where the passages support the answer, and make insufficient variants by deleting the sentence that contains the answer span, repeating the deletion using 5 different random choices of neighboring sentences to remove. Let Llama-3.1-70B-Instruct answer all versions, compute E from the log-likelihood gain of the passages and I from the closed-book log-likelihood, and retrain a logistic detector on the sufficient versions for 10 seeds. Apply each retrained detector to the insufficient versions and report AUROC, F1 and the shift of E and I between versions, averaged over the retrainings.
CONTROLS: Compare against mean token entropy, response perplexity given the passages, and a ReDeEP reproduction with its published head and layer choices. Score a variant where a random sentence is removed instead of the key one.
COST: 48
PREDICTION: E should drop and I should rise on the insufficient versions, with detection AUROC staying above 0.70; it could fail when the 70B model's memory happens to be right and its answers are labeled supported.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Leave-one-dataset-out transfer of a head-free hallucination detector
PROPOSAL: Compute E as the response log-likelihood gain from the retrieved context and I as the closed-book response log-likelihood, with Llama-3.1-8B as scorer, on 4 datasets: RAGTruth, HaluEval question answering, a data-to-text set built from WebNLG tables, and a news summarization set. Train a logistic regression on 3 datasets and test on the fourth, rotating the held-out dataset, and compare with training on the held-out dataset itself. Also score responses written by GPT-4-class systems where the dataset provides them, to test generators other than the scorer. Report AUROC and F1 for all 4 rotations.
CONTROLS: Compare against mean token entropy, response perplexity given the context, a ReDeEP reproduction with per-dataset head and layer tuning, and a judge-prompt baseline. Ablate E and I separately, drawing splits within datasets with 5 seeds.
COST: 200
PREDICTION: Transfer should cost about 5 AUROC points relative to in-dataset training, far less than the tuning-dependent ReDeEP; it could fail on WebNLG, where the labels follow a different definition of unsupported.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Within-dataset detector at scale with a 70B scorer on RAGTruth
PROPOSAL: Compute E as the response log-likelihood gain from the retrieved context and I as the closed-book response log-likelihood, with Llama-3.1-70B-Instruct as scorer, on the RAGTruth question-answering split over 5 repeated stratified resplits of the response-level labels. Fit a logistic regression and a small gradient-boosted classifier on the signals for each resplit, and add 4 context-corruption variants (shuffled, truncated, sentence-dropped, entity-swapped) to measure how E and I respond. Report AUROC and F1 for both classifiers on the resplits, and the mean response of E and I to the 4 corruptions.
CONTROLS: Compare against mean token entropy, response perplexity given the context, a ReDeEP reproduction with published head and layer choices, and a judge-prompt baseline. Ablate E and I separately; use 10 seeds for the classifier fit.
COST: 200
PREDICTION: The gradient-boosted classifier should lead the logistic regression by under 2 AUROC points; it could fail because 70B closed-book likelihood is dominated by fluency, compressing I.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Span-level validation of E and I against human support annotations
PROPOSAL: Take 200 RAGTruth responses with span-level annotations marking unsupported text, and compute token-level E (log-likelihood gain from the retrieved context) and token-level I (closed-book log-likelihood) with Llama-3.1-8B. Test whether tokens inside annotated spans show a lower E and a higher I than tokens outside them, using a paired comparison within each response and a rank-based effect size. Then check that removing the annotated spans' supporting passage sentence lowers E on the surrounding tokens. Report the effect sizes with bootstrap intervals from 1000 resamples and the token-level AUROC of the ratio of I to E.
CONTROLS: Compare against token entropy and the attention mass on passage tokens as indicators of the same spans, and against a random assignment of spans of equal length within each response. Use 3 seeds for the bootstrap.
COST: 24
PREDICTION: Annotated tokens should show a lower E and a higher I with a medium effect size; it could fail on short spans of 1 to 2 tokens, where token-level log-likelihood is dominated by word frequency.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Span-level validation of E and I across scorers and token windows
PROPOSAL: Take 200 RAGTruth responses with span-level annotations marking unsupported text, and compute token-level E (log-likelihood gain from the retrieved context) and token-level I (closed-book log-likelihood) with scorers from 7B to 70B. Test whether tokens inside annotated spans show a lower E and a higher I than tokens outside them, using 12 smoothing windows from 1 to 24 tokens and a rank-based effect size per scorer and per width. Report the effect sizes with bootstrap intervals, the token-level AUROC of the ratio of I to E, and how the best width changes with scorer size.
CONTROLS: Compare against token entropy and the attention mass on passage tokens as indicators of the same spans, and against a random assignment of spans of equal length within each response. Use 10 seeds for the bootstrap.
COST: 24
PREDICTION: Annotated tokens should show a lower E and a higher I with a medium effect size at most widths; it could fail on short spans of 1 to 2 tokens, where log-likelihood is dominated by word frequency.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Passage-level leave-one-out for E and a closed-book probe for I in multi-passage retrieval
PROPOSAL: When the retriever returns 5 passages of about 150 words, measure E by the response log-likelihood drop under leave-one-passage-out and take the largest drop as the evidence the answer relied on, and take I from the closed-book log-likelihood. Use Mistral-7B-Instruct on HaluEval question answering and RAGTruth question answering with 1000 sampled items, where the gold passage position is shuffled at random. Fit a logistic regression on E, I and the gold-passage drop, and report AUROC and F1. Check that the leave-one-out signal finds the gold passage in at least 70 percent of correct answers.
CONTROLS: Compare against attention-based passage attribution, mean token entropy, response perplexity given the passages, and a ReDeEP reproduction with published head and layer choices. Run 3 seeds for the passage shuffle and drop I in turn.
COST: 120
PREDICTION: Leave-one-out should rank the gold passage first in about 75 percent of supported answers; it could fail when two passages state the same fact and removing either leaves the answer intact.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Leave-one-out and subset removal with a 70B scorer for a single dataset
PROPOSAL: When the retriever returns 5 passages, measure E by the response log-likelihood drop under leave-one-passage-out, pairs of passages removed, and triples removed, and take I from the closed-book log-likelihood. Use a 70B instruction-tuned model on RAGTruth question answering with 1000 sampled items, where the gold passage position is shuffled at random over 5 different shuffles. Fit a logistic regression on E, I and the gold-passage drop, and report AUROC and F1 averaged over the shuffles. Check that the leave-one-out signal finds the gold passage in at least 70 percent of correct answers and compare with the pair and triple removals.
CONTROLS: Compare against attention-based passage attribution, mean token entropy, response perplexity given the passages, and a ReDeEP reproduction with published head and layer choices. Run 10 seeds for the regression and drop I in turn.
COST: 120
PREDICTION: Leave-one-out should rank the gold passage first in about 75 percent of supported answers; it could fail when two passages state the same fact and removing either leaves the answer intact.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Fine-tuned detector head on token-level E and I features from an 8B scorer
PROPOSAL: Extract token-level E (log-likelihood gain from the context) and token-level I (closed-book log-likelihood) from Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct for responses in RAGTruth and train a small 2-layer transformer head over the sequence of paired values to predict the response-level label. Train on responses from 3 generators in RAGTruth and test on 3 other generators and on HaluEval question answering and news summarization sets. Report AUROC and F1 per target, and compare the learned head with the logistic regression on pooled features to see what the sequence model adds.
CONTROLS: Compare against pooled logistic regression, mean token entropy, response perplexity given the context, a ReDeEP reproduction with per-dataset tuning, and a judge-prompt baseline. Shuffle token order inside responses as a control; use 5 seeds for the head training.
COST: 400
PREDICTION: The sequence head should beat pooled features by about 3 AUROC points in-domain and keep 2 of them in transfer; it could fail by fitting generator-specific style in the training split.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Retraining a sequence detector head across scorers on one split
PROPOSAL: Extract token-level E (log-likelihood gain from the context) and token-level I (closed-book log-likelihood) from 5 scorers spanning 7B to 70B parameters for responses in RAGTruth and train a 4-layer transformer head over the sequence of paired values to predict the response-level label, with 10 runs per scorer from different seeds. Train and test on the standard RAGTruth split with 20 percent of responses held out. Report AUROC and F1 averaged over the retrainings, and compare the learned head with the logistic regression on pooled features.
CONTROLS: Compare against pooled logistic regression, mean token entropy, response perplexity given the context, a ReDeEP reproduction with per-dataset tuning, and a judge-prompt baseline. Shuffle token order inside responses as a control; keep the held-out responses fixed.
COST: 400
PREDICTION: The sequence head should beat pooled features by about 3 AUROC points at all scorer sizes; it could fail by fitting generator-specific style in the training split.
